title: Piecewise functions and the IIS tools

questions.heading: Piecewise Writes y Below, Above or Equal to f(x), and the Side Must Match the Push
questions.stem: A model minimizes cost, and a cost variable c follows a concave piecewise curve of hours h (a volume discount). Which Piecewise call makes c the curve's true cost and solves with appsi_highs?

options.says: UB states c <= f(h); with c pushed down the discount model paid 0 for 40 hours whose curve cost is 1,150.
Concave with UB becomes plain rows c <= each line, which put no floor under a cost pushed down.
Right: c >= f(h) with a binary formulation, as 'discount, LB, INC' paid the curve's 870 for 26 months.
Concave with LB keeps the formulation, and the default writes SOS2, which HiGHS refused.

questions.heading: A Convex Cost Bounded From Below Needs No Binaries
questions.stem: A cost curve is convex, minimized, and written with pw_constr_type='LB' and no pw_repn argument. What happens when appsi_highs solves the model?

options.text: HiGHS refuses it, since the default writes SOS2
options.says: For convex with LB, Pyomo replaced the formulation by plain rows before any SOS2 was written; the first line of the table solved.

options.text: It solves only after force_pw=True is added
options.says: force_pw=True keeps the SOS2 formulation, and that is the case HiGHS refused.

options.text: It solves, since HiGHS accepts SOS2 constraints
options.says: HiGHS's Pyomo interface has no SOS constraints: 'Highs interface does not support SOS constraints'.

options.text: It solves, since Pyomo writes one row per segment
options.says: Right: Pyomo saw a convex curve with LB and wrote the three rows c >= each line, with no binaries and no SOS2.

questions.heading: The MIS Tool Explains an Infeasible Model With Any Solver, on Its LP Relaxation
questions.stem: A MILP is infeasible only because a must-do project's single-year cost cannot fit in either year's budget; its LP relaxation, which may split the project, is feasible. What does compute_infeasibility_explanation with HiGHS do?

options.text: It names the must-do row and the two budget rows
options.says: Those three rows are the MILP's IIS, which write_iis gets from a commercial solver; the MIS tool works on the relaxation.

options.text: It raises, reporting that it found no conflict at all
options.says: Right: the tool makes every variable real, so it explains the LP relaxation; on the $4,000k cut it said the model was feasible.

options.text: It returns an empty MIS, since HiGHS has no IIS
options.says: The tool needs no IIS from the solver; it found a 4-row MIS with HiGHS on the $2,600k cut.

options.text: It raises, since it needs CPLEX, Gurobi or Xpress
options.says: That requirement is write_iis's; the MIS tool runs with any solver, HiGHS here.
